title: Adversarial noise embedset regression harness
summary: Working harness and dataset recipe for embedding regression detection that focuses on adversarial/noise perturbations and multilingual anchor stability. Designed for onboarding new embedding models and catching brittle failure modes not visible in standard smoke tests.
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a pragmatic evaluation harness and a set of curated and synthetic embedsets intended to surface regressions caused by noise sensitivity, tokenization drift, quantization side-effects, and cross-lingual inconsistencies when onboarding embedding models into Redwood's semantic search and clustering pipelines. The goal is fast, reproducible checks that complement existing multilang cluster sanity and relevance tests.

Why this matters:
- Standard retrieval/cluster tests can miss brittle failure modes (e.g., a model that returns good average MRR but catastrophically fails on OCR/noise variants).
- In production, user inputs vary (typos, punctuation loss, mixed scripts). Small embedding shifts can cascade into big downstream UX regressions.

Overview of the harness:
1) Base embedset composition: a mix of production-like short queries, multi-sentence docs, and pairwise anchors spanning four domains: docs, helpdesk Q/A, product descriptions, and multilingual FAQ entries. Each anchor group contains 1000 base items where feasible (smaller bilingual anchors at 300–500).
2) Synthetic perturbations: six deterministic transforms applied to each base item to create adversarial variants: token-drop (remove 5–15% tokens), punctuation-strip, OCR-noise (confuse 0/1/5 character classes), randomized casing, numeral-scale (replace numbers with scaled values), and controlled paraphrase (simple templated paraphrasing).
3) Translation pivots: for multilingual stability checks we create pivot-translated variants: source -> pivot (English) -> target and direct source->target where possible to detect translation asymmetry. Languages: en, es, fr, de, zh, pt, ja.
4) Anchor-style bilingual pairs: curated translation pairs (human-verified) used to measure cross-lingual retrieval stability under noise.
5) Negative mining set: in-domain hard negatives harvested from product logs and artificially generated near-neighbors using lexical overlap heuristics.

Evaluation steps (harness):
- Step A: Embed generation: run candidate model on full augmented embedset with identical preprocessing as platform runtime (tokenization flags, normalization). Export embeddings in float32 and (if model supports) int8 quantized representations.
- Step B: Distribution checks: compute per-slice cosine similarity distributions for: base vs base, base vs noisy, base vs translated-pivot, and base vs paraphrase. Run KS-test and compute JS divergence between candidate and baseline distributions.
- Step C: Retrieval metrics: run k-NN retrieval (k=10) on anchor queries and compute MRR@10, MAP@10, NDCG@10, and Recall@1/5. Separate numbers for plain and noisy variants.
- Step D: Clustering sanity: run spherical k-means (k set by label count) and compute silhouette score, cluster purity, and normalized mutual information (NMI) across base and noisy variants. Also compute centroid drift (cosine distance between baseline and candidate centroids).
- Step E: Stability probes: for each perturbation type, compute pairwise embedding cosine degradation (mean and percentile). Report the fraction of items that fall below a degradation threshold (e.g., cosine drop > 0.08).

Key datasets included in this harness (short names):
- prod-anchors: short user queries + canonical response (derived from anonymized logs)
- faq-multilang: multilingual FAQ pairs with human translations (300 per lang)
- docs-desc: product descriptions across categories (longer form, 800 items)
- escore-hardneg: curated hard negatives and lexical near-neighbors (1,200 items)
- synth-noise variants are generated from the base sets on-the-fly by the harness

Metrics and signals we compute (reporting columns):
- baseline_MRR@10, candidate_MRR@10, delta_MRR (pct)
- baseline_NDCG@10, candidate_NDCG@10, delta_NDCG
- silhouette_base, silhouette_candidate, delta_silhouette
- mean_cosine_shift (base->candidate), cosine_shift_p50, p95_drop_fraction
- JS_divergence_distribution, KS_pvalue
- centroid_mean_cosine_move (by cluster)
- crosslingual_anchor_recall@1/5 (per language pair)

Thresholds that trigger automated alerts (suggested):
- delta_MRR@10 <= -0.03 (i.e., drop of 3% or worse)
- delta_NDCG@10 <= -0.04
- delta_silhouette <= -0.02
- mean_cosine_shift >= 0.015 (direction: absolute mean shift)
- JS_divergence_distribution >= 0.025 or KS p-value < 0.01
- centroid_mean_cosine_move >= 0.05 for > 10% clusters
- noise-sensitive failure: fraction of items with cosine drop >0.08 >= 0.05 (5%)
These thresholds are starting points; product teams may tighten them for stricter SLAs.

Quick triage checklist when a regression fires:
- Confirm identical preprocessing: tokenizer version, special-token handling, lowercasing/normalization flags.
- Check quantization path: was int8 used for inference? Compare float32 outputs.
- Review release notes and PRs touching tokenizer, tokenizers lib, or subword vocabulary (link to latest PRs).
- Run a small sample of problematic examples through baseline and candidate and inspect tokenization/embedding differences.
- If noise-specific failures: run ablation by toggling transforms to localize the perturbation type that causes the drop (OCR vs punctuation vs token-drop).
- If multilingual mismatch: test direct vs pivot translations to determine if failure is model-intrinsic or translation asymmetry.
- Check batch size and deterministic seeds; randomness in KV cache or attention kernels can cause tiny drift that accumulates for long docs.

Operational notes for onboarding a new model:
- Run the full harness with candidate and baseline (baseline typically latest production embed model). Save all artifacts with timestamped IDs.
- Store per-example embeddings to enable per-item regression debugging (retention policy: 90 days compressed).
- Auto-generate a regression digest (top 20 worst-impacted items, per-slice metrics, and suggested troubleshooting bullets).
- For models that pass numeric thresholds but show high human-identified failures, trigger a manual eval: sampling of 200 items across affected slices for human relevance judgments.

Examples of failure modes we observed historically (notes):
- Model A: passed average MRR but failed heavily on OCR-noise variants; root cause: new tokenizer aggressive merging removed punctuation tokens that anchored short queries.
- Model B: small NDCG drop but big cluster drift for product descriptions due to different pre-normalization (no L2 normalize before index) leading to cosine magnitude shifts.
- Model C: apparent cross-lingual recall drop traced to translation pivot inconsistency (en->zh translations used different tokenizers during translation pipeline).

Implementation pointers and reproducibility:
- Harness code lives in embeddings-eval-harness repo. Use the harness docker image tag: embeddings-eval:2025-02-01 for repeatability.
- Use deterministic RNG seeds for synthetic transforms. Log the seed per run and include it in the run artifact metadata.
- Store per-run manifest: model_commit, tokenizer_version, inference_flags (normalize, quantize, dtype), dataset_shas.

Next steps and open questions:
- Decide on retention for per-item artifacts and whether to persist paraphrase variants long-term (disk cost vs debugging value).
- Add an OCR-realistic dataset using scanned support tickets (need privacy review).
- Tune thresholds per domain (short queries vs long docs often need different tolerances).

References and notes for reviewers: see linked artifacts above and ping #eng-applied-ml on Slack for review requests.
